founding_year.basis: TechCrunch 2022-09-22: 'founded in 2019 by Sebastian Pollok and Robert Lacher'; Deutsche Startups 2019-04-15 reports the firm forming ('entsteht derzeit') with a EUR 70M target; the adviser's owners date from late 2018 (Form ADV Schedule A: Lacher managing director since 12/2018 via Kensington Beteiligungs GmbH, member 10/2018; Pollok since 03/2019 via Cape Ventures GmbH)

history.value: Visionaries Club was founded in Berlin in 2019 by Robert Lacher, a founding partner of La Famiglia, and Sebastian Pollok, a co-founder of Amorelie, with successful founders and industrial family businesses as its investors. It backed Choco, Xentral and Tacto early and later Miro, Pigment, n8n, Lovable and Black Forest Labs. In 2022 it raised €350 million for its second seed and growth funds and launched Visionaries Tomorrow for deep tech.
history.basis: Founders and their prior companies: Deutsche Startups 2019-04-15 (Lacher 'zuletzt La Famiglia', Pollok Amorelie co-founder); the founder and family-business LP model: TechCrunch 2022-09-22 and the firm's homepage; the named companies are members of the portfolio with cited entries (Choco 2019, Xentral 2021, Tacto 2020 pre-seed; Miro, Pigment, n8n 2025, Lovable 2025, Black Forest Labs 2025); fund generation II: EUR 150M seed + EUR 200M early growth, and the EUR 50M Tomorrow fund (TechCrunch 2022-09-22; Deutsche Startups 2024-02-29 gives Tomorrow a EUR 80M target). Not in the paragraph: the first generation (two funds, EUR 100M by Nov 2020, Deutsche Startups 2020-11-30), the single-company Late Growth vehicles, the 2026 rebrand to 'Visionaries' and move to a GP-led team (Deutsche Startups 2026-08-07), and Judith Dada's move to Langdock as co-CEO (June 2026) while staying a senior partner.

investment_concept.value: “In this era of upheaval, obsession beats playbooks, ambition beats size and conviction beats consensus.”
investment_concept.basis: The firm's own words: the first sentence of the homepage headline (h1), read 2026-09-30; the h1 continues 'We back those who run toward the fire and follow one simple rule: connecting the top 0.1% with the top 0.1%.' Competing lines on the same site: the title-tag tagline 'Hungry Beats Big' and the manifesto heading 'The Visionaries Era: Hungry beats big.' Only the quotation marks were added.

investment_stage.basis: the fund architecture: a seed fund and an early-growth fund 'from Series B onwards' (TechCrunch 2022-09-22), Visionaries Tomorrow for pre-seed and seed deep tech, single-company Late Growth vehicles; the landed entry stages: Seed 18, Pre-Seed 12, Growth 11, Series A 10, undetermined 25 of 76

investment_geo.basis: offices in Berlin and London (the firm's contact section); the landed portfolio's hq_country: DE 30, GB 19, FR 4, CH 3, ES 3, NL 2, SE 2, BE 2, NO 1, HU 1 (67 European rows) and US 9, of 76 -> core Europe, other US (two-label cap respected)

investment_scope.basis: the firm's own description ('investing in B2B tools and AI', homepage meta description; Visionaries Tomorrow: industrial deep tech); focus from the grind's per-row focus column, the five sectors above the 5-company threshold: AI & Applied AI 22, SaaS 18, Fintech & Payments 12, Industrial & Robotics 10, Climate & Energy 7 (then Healthcare & Bio 3, DevTools & APIs 2, Consumer & Marketplaces 1, Security 1)

investment_range.basis: median: press-based, the median of 43 documented entry rounds of the firm's members 2019-2026 (each cited on its row; non-USD sizes at the ECB rate of the round's date) = $10.0M, not a Form D distribution (the companies file none); the 26 pre-seed and seed entries alone have a $5.2M median; lower: the smallest documented entry round it led, Hakuna's EUR 1.5M pre-seed (2021-12-10) = $1.7M; upper: the largest rounds it led or co-led (Solve Intelligence $40M Series B, 2025; PAVE Space $40M seed, 2026) capped at a 15% single-position concentration of its largest fund (Growth Fund II, EUR 200M = $197.7M) = about $30M

notable_investments.basis: The five best known of the firm's own companies, most recognised first (PRO-152). Considered next: TrueLayer, Choco, H Company. Personio, which the firm lists, is out of the portfolio as a partner-carried La Famiglia deal (decisions.md R1).
